solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put in case what is needed for card games

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stow things in a suitcase or box

definitions.text: what is needed for card games
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a full set of playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone advises packing the essentials for an evening of card games.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means filling luggage for travel, and the noun is a complete deck of fifty-two playing cards.

clue.text: Home crops — limited space for horses

parts.note: a pad is informal slang for where someone lives
to dock is to cut short, as with a tail, so crops means docks

explanation.surface: A farm notice listing the homestead, the harvest and an enclosure for the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crops' looks like a noun for harvests, but here it is a verb meaning cuts short, as a horse's tail is docked.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fenced fields near stables where horses graze or are exercised are called by this name.

clue.text: Boss sacks one kitchen worker

indicators.note: to sack is to dismiss from a job, so something gets thrown out of the word

parts.note: the chief is the person in charge
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A manager fires one of the restaurant's kitchen staff.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIEF loses its I to leave CHEF; the surface boss sacking a worker is the deletion itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook employed in a restaurant or hotel kitchen is the standard name for this worker.

clue.text: People leaving money behind in trucks?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: customers who leave a gratuity for staff
second meaning: lorries whose load bed tilts to dump their cargo

explanation.surface: Drivers leave cash behind in their lorries, perhaps as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipper truck tips its load out, which is a second kind of leaving something behind; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous diners who add gratuities and dumping lorries that tilt their beds both carry this name.

clue.text: Article is on origin of mystical belief system

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece being on another means it sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the definite article
taken as written

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of mystical

explanation.surface: A newspaper article discusses where a mystical belief system came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in a god or gods is a broad religious position, matching a system of faith.

clue.text: They seriously think hip-hop losers will regroup

indicators.note: to regroup is to gather again in a new formation, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Musicians who lost out in the hip-hop scene will regroup and think hard about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a defeated band reforming, but the musicians are only letters to be reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinkers who reason deeply about existence, knowledge and ethics are described as people who ponder in earnest.

clue.text: One written to by St Paul, man going after wandering sheep

definitions.text: One written to by St Paul

indicators.note: sheep that are wandering have strayed out of their places, so the letters move about
going after means following, so the man's name is placed behind the other piece

parts.note: the letters of sheep rearranged
Ian is a common man's name

explanation.surface: A shepherd sets off after his straying flock, with a nod to St Paul's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul wrote an epistle to the church at Ephesus; any member of it qualifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's New Testament letter to the Ephesians was addressed to the Christians of the ancient city of Ephesus.

clue.text: Just right, just right, OK?

parts.note: 'just so' means exactly correct, and so alone can mean true, as in 'is that so?'
the same piece again

explanation.surface: Someone checks twice that everything is exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition gives the doubled word; the question mark hints at doubt, matching an answer that means merely passable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only passable, neither good nor bad, is described as mediocre or merely okay.

clue.text: A male in charge, having less feeling as a scientific figure

parts.note: taken as written
a tom is a male animal, especially a cat
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge
more numb, with less sensation

explanation.surface: A man in a position of authority grows emotionally colder as a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER here is read as numb plus -er, not the counting word, though the full answer then uses the counting sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The count of protons in an atom's nucleus is a key value in chemistry and physics.

clue.text: Hostess died — he sadly washes up

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: After the hostess's death, a grieving man is left alone to clean up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning the plates, pans and cutlery after a meal is the household chore meant by the phrase.

clue.text: Mums participating in drama sometimes

indicators.note: participating in means taking part inside something, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: found straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Mothers sometimes take part in amateur dramatics.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma is an informal word for a mother, so the plural stands for several mothers.

clue.text: Island's heavenly sign when corn has been cut

indicators.note: something that has been cut has had a portion removed, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: Capricorn is a sign of the zodiac, and a constellation in the sky
taken as written

explanation.surface: An island's emblem is a star sign showing a harvest after the corn is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing CORN from the end of CAPRICORN leaves the island; 'Island's' reads as 'Island is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This rocky Italian isle in the Bay of Naples is a famous holiday resort.

clue.text: Dan and Peter, badly brought up

indicators.note: badly suggests something done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters of the two names; 'and' just joins them

explanation.surface: Two boys, Dan and Peter, had a poor upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly brought up' reads as one phrase, but badly is the anagram signal and only 'brought up' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised as a child by a mother or father, or cared for as their offspring, is the sense.

clue.text: Room for service personnel in a port

parts.note: a mess is where members of the armed forces eat and socialise
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers' quarters are found in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a port' looks like a location phrase, but IN and A are pieces and only port defines.
explanation.definitionFit: This Sicilian city on the strait facing mainland Italy is a busy seaport and ferry harbour.

clue.text: Excited mate's holding your old gemstone

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so one piece goes within the other
someone excited cannot keep still, so these letters jump into a new order

parts.note: the letters of mate's, the apostrophe ignored
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An eager friend clutches a precious stone that once belonged to you.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple variety of quartz prized as a semi-precious stone in jewellery.

clue.text: Musical section in street bands

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a ring is a circular band, such as one worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A section of musicians plays in the street with marching bands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' wants to be groups of musicians, which fits the surface; here they are circles of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Violins, violas, cellos and basses form one of the main sections of an orchestra.

clue.text: Deliberately avoided day away from home

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
out means not at home

explanation.surface: Someone dodged a commitment by spending a day out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosing not to take part in a dance, game or activity is to stay on the sidelines for it.

clue.text: Church pursuing writer for money

indicators.note: pursuing means chasing behind, so the church piece follows the other one

parts.note: a pen is something you write with
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church is chasing an author for payment.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is the thing that writes, a common crossword stretch of writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennies are small British coins, and their plural refers to sums of cash in general.

clue.text: Wood that may be used for burning when hard

definitions.text: Wood that may be used for burning

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tip that firewood burns best once it has hardened.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue looks like the definition, but only the first six words define; the last two build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree's timber is famous firewood that burns well even when green, so it suits fuel.

clue.text: Worker may be bananas

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a manual labourer, as on a farm or ship
second meaning: a cluster of bananas growing together

explanation.surface: A worker may be crazy, since bananas is slang for mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' wants to mean mad; it is the fruit, which grows in clusters with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhand or deckhand is a labourer, and a bunch of bananas on the stalk is called this too.

clue.text: Box carried by his partner

indicators.note: something carried by these words is held inside them, so the letters lie within

parts.note: found straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A box is lugged along by a man's companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to practise boxing lightly with a partner, throwing punches without full force.

clue.text: A life of someone by himself?

definitions.text: A life of someone by himself?

parts.words: A life of someone by himself?
parts.note: surface reading: a solitary existence, a person living alone

parts.words: A life of someone by himself?
parts.note: setter's reading: a written life story whose author is its own subject

explanation.walkthrough: 'By himself' suggests loneliness, but 'by' names the author, as in a book by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A book recounting a person's own life, written by that same person, is the literary genre meant.

clue.text: French editor celebrated, ultimately fantastic editor

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: final letter of celebrated

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word, taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrated French editor is praised as ultimately fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' seems to modify fantastic, but it picks the last letter of celebrated before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot edited the great eighteenth-century Encyclopédie, the landmark work of the French Enlightenment.

clue.text: Left-winger to run

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short for Trotskyist, a far-left socialist
second meaning: to move at a jogging pace

explanation.surface: A socialist decides to stand for office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' suggests standing in an election, which suits a left-winger; it is the gentle jogging pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Trotsky's revolutionary politics, and a pace between walking and running, share this short word.
